newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close 3.31 pct up on govt measures.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close 3.31 pct up on govt measures.

text.p: Thai stocks closed 3.31 percent higher on Wednesday as local investors bought large capitalised bank, finance and energy issues after a portion of market support fund began buying on its first day, brokers said.
The SET index rose 19.09 points to 596.19 on brisk 6.3 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 1.73 points to 43.87.

"Local investors were active in the market today as they bought cheap, large capitalised stocks for speculative reasons. They entered the market after hearing that a support fund amounting to one billion baht began investing in the market today," said Samart Rusmeerojwong of James Capel Asia.
The one billion baht is part of the 50 billion baht market support fund Thai commercial banks had volunteered to pool to help the battered market whose index had plunged 15 percent this month.
Krung Thai Bank Plc, the administrator of the fund, declined to confirm that the fund began buying today.

"According to the Thai Bankers Association's resolution, one billion (baht) would be made available on Thursday but Krung Thai Bank is allowed to start buying today. We can place orders now and settle up to three working days later," Krung Thai Bank Senior Vice President Dusit Tengniyom told Reuters.

The market sentiment was further boosted by a U.S. Federal Reserve Board decision not to raise interest rates along with comments made on Monday by the central bank governor that Thai exports rose 4.8 percent year on year in March, brokers said.
Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Monday Thai exports rose 4.8 percent year-on-year in March and averaged 4.4 percent growth during the first four months.
All key sectors advanced on Wednesday with the banking sector gaining the most in terms of value, rising 5.17 percent.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, gaining four baht to 108. Banpu, in the energy sector, rose four to 356.
